calls.message: Build a Markdown Note-Taking CLI. Subcommands: new, list, show, edit, delete. Store notes as .md files with YAML frontmatter in ~/.note-taker/. Search by tag or keyword. Single file note_taker.py, stdlib only.
calls.result:
The spec is written and lints clean (100/100), but nothing is built yet. It's a spec-only bundle with no Dafny, because this isn't critical logic. It lives at `forgemyspec-bundle/note-taker/`.

**Obligations (all boundary tests):**

| id | what it checks |
|---|---|
| `new_writes_note` | `new` writes `<id>.md` with YAML frontmatter into the notes directory, creates the directory if missing, and gives colliding titles distinct ids |
| `show_roundtrip` | `show` returns the title, tags and body that `new` stored |
| `list_and_search` | `list` shows all notes; `--tag` and `--search` return only matching notes |
| `edit_and_delete` | `edit` runs `$EDITOR` and rejects broken frontmatter; `delete` removes only the named note; unknown ids exit 1 |
| `single_file_stdlib` | `note_taker.py` is one file and imports only standard-library modules |

**Assumptions I made (tell me if any are wrong):**
- The notes directory is `~/.note-taker/`, and `NOTE_TAKER_DIR` overrides it so tests never touch your home.
- Frontmatter holds `id`, `title`, `tags` and `created`. The script reads and writes this small YAML subset itself, since PyYAML isn't in the standard library.
- A note's id is its slug, which is also the filename (`<id>.md`).
- `edit` opens `$EDITOR`, then `$VISUAL`, then `vi`.
- `--search` is a case-insensitive substring match on title and body; `--tag` is a case-insensitive exact match.
